# Setup Project Verification

For UI connections, discover available `impeccable`, `fixing-accessibility` and,
only for React/Next.js impact, `vercel-react-best-practices`. Link project intent,
states, responsive and keyboard criteria to existing token/component owners.
Actually [execute the guide](references/project-verification.md#execute-and-repair-the-existing-guide),
including cleanup; a written command or registry row is not a connected result.

For each requested connection, use [task verification](references/project-verification.md#task-verification) to select new-feature, bug-fix or behavior-preservation criteria before execution. Connect both relevant executable checks and business/architecture reviews at the actual FE/API/Domain owners; an affected layer connection needs normal and failure-path persistence/fresh-read evidence, not a set of layer PASS results.

Read [shared verification responsibilities](references/project-verification.md). Inspect existing project guidance, requirements, package/native commands, callers, fixtures and UI sources before adding anything. Distinguish first connection from reuse; identify exactly which pilot/project connections are absent. Preserve underlying product requirements.

1. For initial whole-project setup, reconcile all functions in the agreed project/revision boundary. For a missing connection in a small task, inspect only that path and its callers. Do not expand it into whole-project initialization. Reconcile the requested scope against requirements, UI/routes, API/CLI, jobs, roles, flags and tests. Partition large maps by user flow with stable IDs. Each Feature links requirements, outcomes/invariants, variants, FE/API/Domain owners, state/data effects, existing guarantees, checks and gaps. Reuse the map/command registry. Use [workflow obligations](references/workflow-obligations.md) for resumable progress and omission detection. Unresolved candidates keep whole-project initialization PARTIAL without blocking independently connected tasks; a first runnable flow confirms execution linkage, not complete mapping. Features without automatic checks remain in the map. Read `mapping_status` separately from overall task status; explicitly retain product-quality/data gaps as `product_findings` without treating their repair as map setup work. Unclassified or missing map content remains a mapping finding.
2. Inspect setup/teardown, pretest/migration and command forwarding for side effects. Identify source/dirty diff, dependencies, synthetic fixture, owned process/build/URL and cleanup. Honor manual capability disables and use the recorded fallback. Do not copy credentials, original DBs or uncommitted files into experiments.
3. Connect Launch → Doctor → Drive → Evidence → Cleanup through existing commands. Follow the shared guide's control/observation discovery: project dependencies first, verified host fallback, actual target, test role/data and retained artifacts. HTTP 200 is readiness only: bind served source/build and launch/process evidence to the checkout. Do not stop an unknown server to obtain its port.
4. Run the actual path, including affected persistence/reload and relevant failure/normal cases. For compatible registered native JSON checks, persist the reviewed assertion specification in the project's existing verification area and connect the bundled CLI's `--prepare` → `--execute` path described in [the execution contract](references/result-viewer.md). The installed plugin supplies its capture script automatically; do not add a project copy or a metadata collector. Reuse the existing adapter for other report formats, or retain native output with an explicit binding gap when no compatible producer exists. Propagate native exit and inspect actual case/skip/error facts; capture records execution and leaves product judgment to the project's adapter/observer.
5. Leave the shortest repeatable execution and read-only bundle lookup commands, including new-output/resume and owned-process cleanup boundaries. Verify the connection actually produces reusable evidence and lookup does not rerun checks. Reuse existing AGENTS/index/guide as the project verify-product and ui-system entrypoints. Add a local Skill only for demonstrated repeated branching that those paths cannot express. Do not force Harness installation.

A connection is complete only when it is committed in the product repository (or the user explicitly declines that commit): an isolated copy, fixture or plugin-side adapter is evidence, not a connection. Keep the registered contract lean: point assertions at observations the project's runner already produces, one entry per Feature outcome, instead of restating every count. Record durable non-applicability in Feature `scope` with its decider, and ask the user for `business_value` (goal plus metric/source, proxy coverage IDs, or a deliberate deferral with who decided and when to reconsider) instead of leaving it unstated.

Use the same failing criterion after a repair and a nearby valid case; equivalent baseline GREEN is appropriate for preserved behavior. Preserve raw failures. If execution is unavailable, record the missing observation, cause, fallback and resume condition, and continue independent connections. Finish only the named verified scope; metadata and generated files do not establish the first actual flow.

Where an architecture boundary or token/visual expectation can be stated mechanically, connect it through the project's existing linter or browser runner as described in [executable guardrails](references/project-verification.md#executable-guardrails-before-semantic-review), and prove the rule rejects a synthetic violation.

Declare applicable full-stack `coverage` on the existing Feature, separating perspectives from responsibility areas and tests from semantic reviews. Connect shared UI `ui_systems` once to existing guide/token/component owners and consumer Feature IDs as described in the shared responsibilities. When no style guide exists, use the existing UI capability to write project-specific design intent and state/responsive/accessibility references from current code, then confirm audit consumes it. Missing owners or guide links remain repair findings; metadata cannot certify visual correctness.
